sourceInformation.source: Raiders of the Lost Ark (Atari 2600, 1982), designed by Howard Scott Warshaw
sourceInformation.perspective: Third-person isometric 3D, with a tracking escape camera
sourceInformation.tech: Three.js 0.180.0 (r180), WebGPURenderer with WebGL 2 fallback, Rapier 3D 0.19.3, Gamepad API, Web Audio API, AI Hub Session Protocol v1 client 1.4.0, PeerJS 1.5.5, BroadcastChannel. Interface fonts: Barlow Condensed and DM Sans.
sourceInformation.artDirection: Stylized cel shading, ink outlines, hand-built low-poly sandstone dioramas, warm paper and teal shadows
sourceInformation.animation: Native Three.js AnimationMixer and AnimationClip keyframes for walk, idle, whip, evade, flute, digging, parachuting and biplane propeller; procedural snake motion and effects
sourceInformation.audio: Original code-synthesized adventure music (10% by default), procedural sound effects, Animalese-style gibberish voices; no audio files
sourceInformation.online: 1–4 player host-authoritative cooperative AI Hub sessions; standalone WebRTC rooms via PeerJS and same-browser BroadcastChannel rooms
sourceInformation.testing: Headless Chromium 153 with Playwright 1.63.0: 33/33 full-suite checks, including the complete seven-chapter playthrough, WebGPU state, WebGL 2 visual review, emulated standard gamepad, touch, offline audio, two-page co-op, direct file launch, and four official AI Hub harness scenarios. A stricter replay regression passed 8/8, showing every chapter and nine whip crossings. Visuals reviewed at 1600x900 and 1920x1080; touch profile 844x390. No FPS targets. Physical controller, real mobile hardware, subjective audio quality and cross-device WebRTC: unknown.
sourceInformation.research: Original Atari instruction manual and reverse-engineered game analysis: inventory, trading, snakes and flute, map room, ankh, mesas, parachute, room silhouettes, enemies and TIA sound / title music. AI Hub Session Protocol v1, Three.js r180 toon material source, and Rapier character-controller documentation. Original audio recordings were not auditioned.

testingFeedback: 10 findings were addressed: 8 game or UX issues and 2 test-tool issues. These included co-op roster synchronization, title loading and attract timing, replay routing, shared Sprite geometry cleanup, canyon visibility, controller scrolling, material colors and an automated evade timing error.
1 critical issue: a newly joined co-op player could lack a visible actor when the roster changed without a room change. It was fixed and two-page state convergence passed.

The two-page authoritative co-op state comparison caught the missing remote actor. The complete seven-chapter scripted playthrough also verified trading, both puzzles, traversal, boss combat, defeat recovery and the escape ending.
The WebGPU screenshot was blank in this headless environment. WebGPU state assertions and WebGL 2 captures provided the useful evidence instead.
engineFeedback: Native toon materials, reusable geometry and AnimationMixer clips made a coherent ink-and-sand world possible without external art or animation files.

Yes. Cloning a toon node material lost the intended cloth colors, and disposing shared Sprite geometry hid later inscriptions. A WebGPU queue-completion diagnostic also failed on the headless adapter. Each was corrected or replaced with an appropriate check.
The adventure state machine, contextual interactions, procedural art and audio, input abstraction, checkpoints, and host-authoritative cooperative networking.
Keeping Rapier movement, animated whip traversal, room transitions and replicated actors synchronized across input methods and network copies.
An integrated character controller and a small gameplay / resource-lifetime inspector would make this kind of single-file game easier to build.
promptFeedback: The specific source, controller-first requirements, complete vertical-slice scope and explicit testing stand-ins gave the game a clear direction.
Standalone networking transport, signaling-service expectations and the target length of the demo were unspecified. There was no blocking ambiguity.
Combining seven distinct adventure sequences, procedural presentation, controller and touch support, and verified standalone / AI Hub co-op in one HTML file.
Specify the standalone networking transport, whether public signaling services are acceptable, and a target demo duration.

aiHub.name: Raiders of the Lost Map
aiHub.tagline: One missing map. Far too many snakes.
aiHub.description: Trade in a bustling bazaar, charm snakes, solve a sunlit atlas, and swing across desert mesas in a cel-shaded pulp adventure. Recover a buried reliquary and outrun the inevitable boulder, solo or with up to three partners.
aiHub.controls: Left stick / WASD move; Square / LMB whip; Triangle / E interact; Cross / Space evade; Circle / F flute or parachute; L1 / Q notes; Options / Esc pause.
